reason: Verified in source and by driving master.html?v=approach&state=owner-editing at 1440. render-b.js move() (lines 228-239) writes exactly four things: data-away, style.top, .b-away and read.textContent. Every other dependent fact is frozen at first paint. Measured: before any press the row reads away 23, date 'Sat 8 Aug' (CSS uppercases it), grab aria-label 'Send the invitations, Saturday 8 August, in 23 days...', readout 'Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 days', horizon gap note 'Nothing is planned for the next 16 days.' After twelve presses of Move a week earlier: away 1, top 14px, and the date is STILL 'Sat 8 Aug', the aria-label is STILL 'in 23 days', the gap note is STILL 'nothing for the next 16 days' while the item is one day out, and the readout reads 'in 1 days' having dropped the date entirely. So a count of 1 sits beside a label saying 8 Aug, and the accessible name contradicts the visible one by 22 days. The collision claim also holds: one press puts invitations at away 16, the same top as the menu tasting, and the adjacency check reports invitations x menu overlapping (the edited row wins on z-index 2, b.css:386, so it covers its neighbour rather than being covered). The finding does not restate the gates: interaction-check.mjs checks proportionality, per-date counts and collisions only at first paint on non-editing states, and its single post-move assertion is readout.includes(String(moved.away)) - which 'in 1 days' passes. Nothing here is taste; every one of these is a factual disagreement the product creates about the one fact a planner is moving.
sharpenedFix: The intent is right, the API in the fix as written is wrong and would not compile against the fixture. There is no F.addDays and F.today is a STRING ('2026-07-16'), not a function - render-b.js already calls F.fmt.medium(F.today). Sharpened: (1) add a date-shift helper to fixture.js beside days()/daysTo(), exported as api.plusDays(iso, n) returning an ISO string via Date.UTC arithmetic, and a pluralising api.fmt.dayCount(n) returning n + (n === 1 ? ' day' : ' days'), so '1 days' can never be typed anywhere again. (2) In render-b.js, lift the grab's accessible name out of measure() into one shared builder grabLabel(title, iso, away) and call it from both first paint (line 76) and move(). (3) In move(), derive var nextIso = F.plusDays(F.today, current) once and write every dependent fact from it: .b-date textContent = F.fmt.weekdayShort(nextIso) + ' ' + F.fmt.short(nextIso); the .b-grab aria-label via grabLabel(); read.textContent = F.fmt.longYear(nextIso) + ' · in ' + F.fmt.dayCount(current). Leave .b-away a bare number - the comment at line 234 is a deliberate decision and the count column's one grammar must not be broken to fix this. (4) The gap note cannot be fixed by 're-running the horizon's gap-note accessor' because no such accessor exists - it is computed inline in horizon() from ahead()[0], which reads the immutable fixture and can never see the move. Extract gapNote(nearestAway) as its own builder, and after each move recompute nearestAway as the minimum of every live .b-item's current away (Number(el.getAttribute('data-away')) falling back to its .b-away) and rewrite .b-gapNote from it, with the singular form and a distinct sentence when the nearest thing is tomorrow. (5) Drop 'Re-run the collision guard after every move, not only at first paint' - there is no collision guard in the renderer; it exists only in interaction-check.mjs. Two items genuinely one day apart MUST touch or the measure stops being proportional, which is the direction's whole thesis, so do not nudge positions. Instead, when the moved item lands within a row height of a neighbour, mark both with a data-crowded attribute that tightens their box and states the shared day in the readout ('Saturday 1 August 2026 · in 16 days · same day as Menu tasting'), so the conflict the planner just created is reported rather than hidden under z-index 2. (6) Gate additions, restated so they are checkable: after three presses assert .b-date, the .b-grab aria-label and .b-stepRead all resolve to F.plusDays(F.today, Number(item.dataset.away)); assert .b-gapNote's number equals the live minimum away; assert no rendered string in the state matches / 1 days /; and assert that when two items share a top the crowded marker is present on both, instead of asserting no collision (which the honest measure cannot promise once an owner moves things together).
